newsitem.title: THAILAND: THAI STOCKS CLOSE SLIGHTLY LOWER, AWAITING IMF.
newsitem.headline: THAI STOCKS CLOSE SLIGHTLY LOWER, AWAITING IMF.

text.p: Thai stocks closed lower on Friday as investors stayed on the sidelines awaiting talks between Thai and IMF officials and on concerns over unsettled orders resulted from the closure of finance firms, brokers said.

"The suspension of finance companies earlier this week had created problems with unsettled orders between some investors and the suspended brokerage houses. Also, investors were waiting for Thai and IMF talks on loans sought by this country," said Issaraphol Kansorn of Wall Street Finance.
The composite SET index closed 1.19 points lower at 636.85 on thin 2.8 billion baht turnover.
The unsettled order problems arose after the government ordered the suspension of 42 ailing finance companies on Tuesday, bringing the total of finance companies suspended to 58 since late June.
Talks between Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya with IMF and Japanese officials on the multi-billion dollar package to help Thailand's battered economy, are scheduled to start on Monday in Tokyo.
Theai Finance Ministry has said that Thailand was likely to seek $13 billion from several financial sources.
Brokers said the market was also sluggish because investors did not want to hold stocks over the weekend.
Investors also preferred to hold cash rather than stocks presently, they said.
Bangkok Bank, Thailand's largest commercial bank, topped the active list, losing three baht to 166. Nava Finance shed 2.25 to 31.00 but Advanced Info gained six to 236.
